cells.tense: Two claims on your hours are both being met, and neither of them is dropping.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Take one piece of the work you'd usually do unseen and do it where the person it's for can watch. Say nothing about it.
cells.core:
There's a direction you're carrying, and what you keep alive is still alive. Two needs pull at your hours and neither one falls — that balance is real work, and from outside it looks like nothing much. The momentum holds because the care holds.

So spend the pen on one of them and bring it into view. Some upkeep you run in the dark — the second pass, the quiet fix — do it where whoever it's for can watch you. No announcement. You don't owe anyone the tally of hours. Let it land in front of them once, then go on with your day. The push and the care were two jobs in your head only, and one piece done openly shows both of you that.
cells.sheetLine: You hold two things going at once, and both keep going.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing, in form, without forcing it
cells.place: On the way to somewhere, keeping direction through the resistance in front of you

cells.tense: By the time this lands you will have mapped every way it could go sideways.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Take something that's already done and be satisfied with it for an hour. Don't touch it, don't start the next thing.
cells.core:
On this push you're standing in a future nobody can write yet — what it'll need, what could slip, what has to be in place. Care runs out past the thing it's for, and the grip shows even when the work is good. People can feel a hand closing on them.

A finished thing doesn't get to stay finished near you. Something is one step from being improved. Take a job, a room, a piece of work that's actually done and let yourself be satisfied with it for an hour. Hands off. No next pass, no plan for the following move. If they drift toward it, put them somewhere else. Sit in the done thing until it registers as done, and you'll see the push was not kept alive by clenching.
cells.sheetLine: The care is racing past the thing it's meant to feed.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing, in form, without forcing it
cells.place: On the way to somewhere, keeping direction through the resistance in front of you

cells.tense: There was a direction you were walking, and you are no longer standing in it.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Take the direction you'd already chosen and follow it one more week — no sign it's working, none needed.
cells.core:
In the push, what you were carrying has gone quiet. The daily upkeep still happens, but the larger direction — the one that was going somewhere — isn't being walked. Energy drained out of it, and effort doesn't pour that back in. Trying harder at the same pace just burns what's left.

Go back to the one you'd already picked, before whatever happened, and follow it a week further. Not a plan. Not a sprint. One week of turning up for it again, with nothing to prove and no sign required that you were right to want it. Hope that's been tested is still hope. Something small and repeated will carry you back into the direction you set down — you don't need to feel ready first.
cells.sheetLine: The direction you set down is still there to walk.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing, in form, without forcing it
cells.place: On the way to somewhere, keeping direction through the resistance in front of you

cells.tense: Something here is being kept going, and if asked you'd say it mostly runs itself.
cells.act: let what you gave up be seen by the people it was for, without a word about it
cells.ask: Next time you give up something for the people this work is for, do it where they can see. Say nothing about it.
cells.core:
On the way to whatever you're working for, there's a hand in it you don't count as yours. Hours handed over, ground yielded, small sacrifices made to keep the balance — and your name isn't on any of it. You file it under how things are. It isn't how things are.

Let one of those go-unders be visible. Some gift you've been making quietly — the smaller room, the covered shift, letting the other one have it — let it happen where they can see. No explaining. No word about what it cost. Just the act out where the light is. Someone watching doesn't make it less generous; it makes it yours. The work has been in your hands, and this is only you looking at them too.
cells.sheetLine: What you give up is yours, but you've filed it under how things are.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing, in form, without forcing it
cells.place: On the way to somewhere, keeping direction through the resistance in front of you
